svg.title: Two problems in the SKF measurement update
svg.desc: Left: prior N(0,1), a likelihood centred at z = 2, the exact posterior N(1, 0.5), and the Gaussian recovered by the truncated Stein system of Section 5.2, N(-0.25, 0.19), on the wrong side of the prior. Right: the refinement loop with exact recovery produces N(1, 0.5), then N(1.33, 0.33), N(1.5, 0.25), N(1.6, 0.2): each pass narrows the posterior and pulls it toward z = 2, as if the same measurement had been observed again.
svg.text: The measurement update as §5.2 writes it, on the simplest case: prior N(0, 1), z = 2, R = 1
Stein recovery, r = 2: the mean moves the wrong way
Refinement, exact recovery: z counted again
Left: with the rows and truncation §5.2 describes, the recovered mean is −0.25. Adding the β = 0 row E[s] = 0, or centring at the posterior mean, gives +1.
Right: the refinement λ ← SM(m⁺) + λ_lik adds the same measurement again on every pass.
